title: PowerToys运行时ALT键松发BUG问题：Alt 物理按下不触发，物理松开立刻触发按下与松开
author: x123ly
summary: Grab and Move intentionally delays Alt keydown while its Alt-absorption option is enabled; the report lacks the foreground and input-transition evidence needed to identify why shortcuts fail.

status.label: Reproduce before designing a fix
status.detail: The reported delayed event is consistent with the enabled Alt-absorption setting, but the separate shortcut failure has no confirmed hook-state branch.

next_action.label: Reproduce locally
next_action.reason: Toggle the shown Alt-absorption setting and capture the exact Alt, mouse, and focus sequence before changing the keyboard hook.

judgment.rationale: No linked pull request, assignment, duplicate designation, or fork implementation covers this report. The screenshot confirms the Alt-absorption setting is enabled, and current code intentionally swallows Alt keydown and replays it later; that explains the observed delayed event but not the reported shortcut failure. No diagnostic archive, foreground application, window mode, or event sequence identifies a defective state transition.
evidence: The reporter identifies Grab and Move enablement as the condition that correlates with the symptom and reports that disabling it removes the problem.
The attached image shows the setting that blocks Alt from interacting with a window menu after drag or resize enabled.
The issue has one automated triage comment, no assignee, no linked pull request, and no diagnostic archive.

src/modules/GrabAndMove/GrabAndMove/main.cpp:KeyboardProc saves and swallows Alt keydown when g_shouldAbsorbAlt is enabled, then replays the modifier through ReplayAbsorbedModifier on another key or Alt keyup.
Related Issue 50248 reports key-up-only trigger-key behavior and includes diagnostics; Issue 49037 reports separate Alt interception conflicts, but neither proves the transition in this report.
judgment.recommended_action: Use the display-only reproduction plan to distinguish expected configured absorption from a shortcut-breaking transition. Do not propose a source change until that sequence is captured.

fix_assessment.rationale: No existing implementation is linked or found in the fork. The only defensible proposed work is a reproduce-first investigation that identifies the exact hook-state transition before an implementation fix is designed.

proposed_fixes.title: Establish the failing Grab and Move hook transition before changing code
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Unconfirmed. The visible delayed Alt keydown is an intended consequence of the enabled g_shouldAbsorbAlt path. The shortcut failure could instead require a stale absorbed-modifier state, a pending mouse interaction, a foreground transition, or application-specific input handling; the report does not distinguish them.
plan: Reproduce with Grab and Move enabled on a current build, comparing the pictured Alt-absorption option enabled and disabled while recording delivered keyboard events and Alt+Tab and Alt+Esc behavior.
Capture the foreground executable, window mode, configured activation modifier, and exact Alt, mouse, and focus-transition sequence at the occurrence.
Capture a PowerToys diagnostic report immediately after reproduction and map the confirmed sequence to KeyboardProc, ReplayAbsorbedModifier, pending interaction state, and foreground-reset handling.
Only after the trace identifies a faulty branch, create a narrow source-change design and regression test for that exact sequence.
verification: Run the recorded sequence with Alt absorption enabled and disabled; establish whether delayed Alt delivery is expected configuration behavior or coincides with failed shortcuts.
For any later fix, verify delivered keydown precedes keyup and Alt+Tab and Alt+Esc work without regressing Grab and Move drag, resize, modifier-click, or disabled-absorption behavior.

confidence.rationale: The relevant hook and intentional delayed-delivery mechanism are directly observed, but no occurrence-specific evidence selects the branch that causes the claimed shortcut failure.

issue_context.summary: The report describes a physical Alt key whose delivered keydown is delayed until release while Grab and Move and FancyZones are enabled, breaking Alt shortcuts in a timing-dependent scenario.
known_information: The report names PowerToys 0.101.2211.0 Preview installed from Microsoft Store.
Grab and Move is the reported enablement-dependent feature; FancyZones was also enabled.
The attached screenshot shows the Alt-absorption setting enabled.
The issue contains one automated triage comment, no assignee, no linked pull request, and no diagnostic archive.
The current Grab and Move hook deliberately stores and suppresses an Alt keydown under g_shouldAbsorbAlt, then injects the delayed keydown through ReplayAbsorbedModifier.
Issue 50248 and Issue 49037 are open related reports, but neither is a linked or confirmed duplicate of this exact occurrence.
inferences: The delayed keydown visible in a keyboard tester may be configured behavior rather than proof of a race.
A stale hook-owned modifier state or foreground interaction may explain the shortcut failure, but application input handling remains an unexcluded alternative.
The FancyZones co-enabled observation is not sufficient to implicate FancyZones without a reproducible inter-module sequence.
issue_context.analysis: An implementation-grade design would be speculative. The report's screenshot and current source agree that Grab and Move can intentionally delay Alt delivery. The claimed loss of Alt+Tab and Alt+Esc would normally require the hook's non-Alt-key replay path or another state transition to fail, but the issue does not record that path. The related diagnostic archive for Issue 50248 establishes a separate trigger-key investigation, not this report's foreground context or configuration.
initial_investigation: Read the live upstream issue body, comment, labels, assignees, timeline, and attached screenshot.
Downloaded and inspected the screenshot; it shows the Alt absorption option enabled.

Downloaded and inspected the related Issue 50248 diagnostic archive, including GrabAndMove settings and logs; it uses Win as the activation modifier and does not provide a trace for this report's Alt scenario.
Inspected src/modules/GrabAndMove/GrabAndMove/main.cpp, including KeyboardProc, ReplayAbsorbedModifier, pending click handling, modifier replay, and foreground-state reset.
Searched current upstream related issue and pull-request traces, local history, and MuyuanMS/PowerToys issue and pull-request traces; no concrete existing fix or Issue 50236 mirror was found.

reproduce.title: Distinguish Alt absorption from a shortcut failure
prerequisites: A keyboard event tester and a switchable foreground application
Ability to toggle the Alt-absorption option shown in the report
setup: Record the current Grab and Move activation modifier and Alt-absorption setting.
Open the target application in its reported window mode and a keyboard event tester.
steps: With Alt absorption enabled, hold and release Alt alone, then try Alt+Tab and Alt+Esc while recording delivered events.
Repeat the same sequence with Alt absorption disabled.
If failure is timing-dependent, repeat while recording mouse buttons, focus changes, foreground application, and window mode.
reproduce.expected_result: The run identifies whether delayed Alt delivery is expected configuration behavior and, if shortcuts fail, captures the exact transition needed for a later hook-state design.
reproduce.setup_prompt: Prepare a current PowerToys build with Grab and Move enabled, a keyboard event tester, and one target application whose window mode can be changed.
